cards.title: Bottom-of-funnel pages beat top-of-funnel content for AI citation
cards.summary: Build specific, high-intent scenario and service pages rather than broad informational content that AI already answers itself.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend limited content budget on a store's blog versus category/product/scenario pages.
steps: Recognize the source's core claim: top-of-funnel informational content is largely wasted effort now because AI overviews answer 'what is X' questions directly, and most small brands lack the authority to shape a narrative on broad terms.

Instead, build pages for concrete scenarios and services your brand actually offers, because high-intent terms are the least searched and therefore the least competitive, even when their ad cost per click is high.

Apply to ecommerce by making category, product, and scenario pages (e.g. replacing 'what is financial reporting' thinking with 'financial reporting software for brick-and-mortar businesses') rather than broad explainer posts.
Niche down further to reduce competition; the source gives the example that the more specific the term, the fewer sites target it properly.

Note the source's caveat: top-of-funnel content can work for brands with an existing audience and authority who introduce a genuinely new point of view, but for most smaller brands the effort is better directed at bottom-of-funnel pages tied to revenue.
caveats: The 'top-of-funnel is a waste' view is the source's opinion, not a measured benchmark; it acknowledges exceptions for high-authority brands.
Bottom-of-funnel claims should still be tested against your own traffic and revenue data.

cards.title: Mine query fan-out language to write on-site copy
cards.summary: Inspect the actual searches an LLM runs, then reuse that exact phrasing in page titles, slugs, H1s and first sentences.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a product, category or landing page's on-page text so the store surfaces in AI-run web searches.
steps: First observe query fan-out visibly in Perplexity, which shows the searches it runs. For ChatGPT, the source describes an advanced method: send a prompt, wait for it to search the web, right-click and inspect, open the Network tab, copy the URL string after '/c', paste it into the filter, refresh, find the orange-bracketed matching entry, open its Response tab, and search that response for the word 'queries' to see the literal searches.
Alternatively, run the prompt a few times and note recurring search phrasings. Search Google for current video walkthroughs, because this interface method may change.
Identify the language the LLM uses to gather information, which often differs from the phrasing of your original prompt.
Transfer that language into your page title, URL slug, H1, and the beginning of your first sentence, since the source argues most websites are extremely bad at tightly targeting language.

Because LLMs constantly trigger web searches, matching their phrasing and holding SEO authority (links and shares) increases the chance its search surfaces your page, letting you control what the model parrots back.
caveats: The source admits the ChatGPT network-tab method is more complicated than Perplexity and may change; verify the current interface before relying on it.
This is a research technique, not a guarantee of citation.

cards.title: Cheap press releases to influence AI answers
cards.summary: Use low-cost newswire distributions with your target phrase repeated in the title, subheading and first sentence to get cited by AI.
cards.use_when: Building brand impressions or correcting/creating an AI-visible narrative about a product, store or founder.
steps: Pick an inexpensive wire service; the source names AB Newswire and cites roughly $80 for a single release, or about $500/year for a package of around 83 releases (about $6 each). Confirm current pricing before budgeting.

Repeat your target phrase in the press release title, subheading, and first sentence. The source cites the example of a 'best-selling SEO book' term placed in all three spots, which later appeared in AI overviews and ChatGPT citations.
Expect the release to syndicate across news sites; the source says AB Newswire distributed into properties like Yahoo News and the Globe and Mail at the time (availability may change).

Use releases for reputation management, company announcements, or local sponsorships (the source gives the example of a local plumbing company sponsoring a little league team) so AI mentions your brand when users ask about it.
The source argues this tactic is durable because real companies rely on press releases, so it is unlikely AI systems stop ingesting them.
caveats: The source describes an experiment that made a fake company appear real; using fake claims risks credibility and legal issues, so apply the tactic only to truthful information.
Distribution networks and pricing change; verify before purchasing.

cards.title: Publish pricing intent to control AI answers about cost
cards.summary: State your pricing or a starting-from figure on your site so AI doesn't invent a number from G2 or Reddit.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to hide pricing on a B2B or high-ticket product page and what to publish instead.
steps: Accept the source's observation: when you ask ChatGPT about B2B SaaS pricing and the site hides it, the model makes something up or pulls it from G2, Reddit or similar third-party sources.

If you want to hide exact pricing, you can still publish a range, e.g. 'starts from $5,000' or 'starts from $50,000'; the source states ChatGPT will then reference your site and say the company doesn't specify pricing but starts from that figure.
Compare outcomes: your own controlled 'starts from' statement is better than the model linking to a Reddit thread complaining that a quote was too expensive.
Apply this to any product or service with variable or quote-based pricing where a wrong AI-stated figure could deter buyers.
Keep the published figure truthful and consistent with your actual sales process.
caveats: Listing a starting price can anchor or filter out some buyers; weigh that against leaving AI to invent a number.
The source's claims about how ChatGPT handles hidden pricing are anecdotal, not a controlled study.

cards.title: Optimize reviews across every platform, not just one
cards.summary: Diversify and monitor your review presence everywhere AI looks, because any single platform can drop out of AI results.
cards.use_when: Managing review profiles and reputation for a store that relies on third-party review sites for AI-driven product comparisons.
steps: Recognize that LLMs search review platforms unprompted. The source notes seeing query fan-out that added 'G2 reviews' for the models' own list of companies, sometimes as the initial fan-out and sometimes after an initial search gathered companies to investigate.
Because platforms can suddenly drop from AI answers (the source cites a period when Reddit fell out of OpenAI's results), don't put all review effort into one platform like G2.

Optimize profiles across the platforms your buyers use, e.g. Trustpilot, Trustpilot alternatives, Yelp and Capterra; ensure the rating is good and the profile description matches what you want to be known for.
Set up review monitoring or alerts so a one-star review on an obscure site can be found and addressed.
Accept you can't prevent bad reviews; ensure good reviews are spread across the board, and the source notes the simplest defense is having a good product.
caveats: You can influence but not fully control third-party reviews.
Which platforms AI cites changes over time, so treat the list as examples, not a fixed checklist.

cards.title: Disclose useful product info on-site so AI doesn't guess
cards.summary: Put pricing, specs and positioning on your own pages so third parties don't define your product in AI answers.
cards.use_when: Deciding what product details to publish versus hide, to control how AI describes your store and products.
steps: The source's framing: GEO comes down to AI parroting whatever you write on your site plus whatever third parties write about your business, so get the parrot to say good things.
Write the accurate product and positioning information you want repeated directly on your own pages.
Encourage mentions on third-party review and affiliate sites that describe your product correctly.
For pricing specifically, publish a range or starting figure even if you keep exact pricing private, so the model cites your site rather than Reddit or G2.
Periodically check what AI says about your products and correct gaps by adding the missing facts to your site.
caveats: This is a principle, not a guarantee AI will cite your page over a popular third-party source.
Inaccurate self-published info that contradicts reality can damage trust once buyers notice.

cards.title: Recognize when SEO has shifted to old-style purchase pages
cards.summary: Google AI mode increasingly cites homepages, category and product pages over listicles, changing what to optimize.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to keep investing in listicle/blog content versus product, category and homepage pages for AI visibility.
steps: Observe, as the source does, that Google AI mode now more often links directly to a brand's homepage or product page rather than a pile of listicles.

Note that in AI results, brand names are often underlined: a solid blue link goes directly to the company site, while a dotted black line opens a new search for the brand name, making the right-hand citations less relevant.
Adapt your store strategy by strengthening products, categories and homepages rather than making a listicle on your own site that competes with the sites Google already sends users to.
The source still advises one acceptable listicle pattern: if you're a toy store, publish e.g. 'top 10 birthday gifts' and position your own products; lists aren't inherently bad.
Expect long-form blog content to carry less weight and put more effort into being recognized elsewhere (reviews, mentions, videos) so Google lists you as a solution for what you sell.
caveats: The shift the source describes is observational and may change; monitor your own AI-visible queries rather than assuming this is permanent.
Different queries and verticals show different behavior; test your specific terms.

cards.title: Do GEO research before touching pages
cards.summary: Find where AI sources its answers for your target prompts, then reverse-engineer your way into those sources.
cards.use_when: Starting an AI-visibility campaign for a store and deciding which channels and pages to prioritize.
steps: Run your target prompts through the LLMs your buyers use, and use query fan-out (visible in Perplexity, or via the response-tab method in ChatGPT) to record which sites AI cites.

If fan-out consistently cites a big retailer or review site for a term you want (the source uses 'best running shoes' and REI as an example), get your brand mentioned on the cited site rather than assuming your own page will outrank it.
Ask your SEO team (internal or agency) for the fan-out of your main keywords; note that some prompt-tracking tools now provide fan-out automatically, and it can also be done manually.
Treat the answer to 'where is the AI getting its information?' as the starting point, then build a plan to appear in those sources.
Repeat the analysis periodically, since which platforms AI favors changes over time.
caveats: Manual fan-out extraction is laborious; the source says sometimes you just have to put in the time.
Fan-out tools and interfaces change; verify current capabilities.

cards.title: Spend 70-80% of GEO effort on good SEO first
cards.summary: Fix technical SEO and build product/service/location pages before chasing off-site AI tactics.
cards.use_when: Allocating budget and team effort across a store's AI-visibility program.
steps: The source's stated split: 70-80% of GEO is good SEO, with the rest building on top of it.
Ensure the website is technically sound.
Create pages for the products and services you offer, and location pages if the business is location-based.
Build content for what you offer, including acceptable list formats that position your own products.

Once SEO is in place, go beyond the site: check who shows up for your target searches and reach out to affiliates and third-party sites to be mentioned, and decide whether video, TikTok, Instagram or community channels matter for your buyers.
Include reputation management and review monitoring in the off-site portion.
caveats: The 70-80% figure is the source's rough estimate, not a measured formula; adapt to your store's maturity.
Off-site tactics depend on resources the source says may come after the basics are covered.

cards.title: Screen growth tactics by your time horizon
cards.summary: Ask what a tactic does to your brand in two or three years before scaling it, especially if you plan to be around long term.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to adopt a fast but risky AI-spam content or link tactic for a store with long-term customers.
steps: Before scaling any tactic, ask: what impact will this have on me in two or three years?
If you run a churn-and-burn site built for short-term gains, the source says some aggressive tactics are an acceptable business model.
If you're a real business with real customers and a 10-15 year plan, the source says you cannot afford tactics that risk an algorithm penalty, even for a short-term gain.
Apply this to AI-spam scaling, templated listicles, and any pattern that a platform could penalize at the domain level.
The source's broader warning: companies that scale spam listicles can get hit algorithmically for a couple of years, which creates an opening for competitors to take their rank.
caveats: This is the source's risk judgment, not a measured penalty probability.
Risk tolerance legitimately varies by business model; the source explicitly allows aggressive tactics for short-term sites.

cards.title: Capture brand impressions from AI answers
cards.summary: Treat logo or link placement beneath AI overviews as paid-ad-equivalent brand exposure, not just lost clicks.
cards.use_when: Evaluating the value of AI overview presence when organic click-through has fallen for a store's queries.
steps: Acknowledge that the traffic top-of-funnel pages got five years ago is gone; AI answers and AI overviews stand between the user and the click.
Look for the residual exposure: AI overviews sometimes include a linked box and your logo, and you can get your brand or site listed right beneath the overview.
Count those impressions as brand exposure, comparable to the impressions companies already pay for on billboards and TV ads.
Use this framing when setting expectations internally or with clients about AI-era traffic, shifting some success measurement from clicks to impressions and branded-search lift.
Combine with on-site conversion work, since the source says listing for a solution or service depends on being recognized for what you do.
caveats: The source frames these impressions as valuable but gives no measurement of their conversion impact; treat the comparison to paid impressions as an analogy, not data.
You may need to track branded search volume and direct traffic to estimate any effect.
